title: Introducing Custom Factory Program
summary: A software factory of agents, built for your codebase and running in your stack.
body_markdown:
Today we're launching our **Custom Factory program** . Our forward-deployed engineers embed with your team and co-build a software factory for your codebase on Mastra, running in your stack.


We know what a factory can do because we run one. Mastra's software factory now handles 70% of our issues, and since we launched it, our PRs have grown 6x. Most of that work starts in Slack with Shipyard, our Slack agent. Anyone on the team can hand Shipyard a bug or a feature request, and the factory takes it from there, all the way to a pull request ready for review.


We built our factory for our organization, centered around Mastra as an open-source project. It's a great starting spot, and most engineering organizations have their own processes. So we're taking the factory as a starting spot, and tailoring it to your organization and your processes.


*Mastra's factory board: issues are triaged, researched and moved from intake to review, with each one scored for impact and effort.*


Most engineering teams are still adopting AI one tool at a time: a coding agent someone runs by hand, an issue investigation agent, a code review agent.


But a factory does the whole thing – it takes work from issue to merged PR. It triages and scopes the task, writes the code, runs the tests, checks its own output, and brings in an engineer where judgment matters. Each step in the pipeline is run by an agent – and it gets better every time it runs.


We've watched other teams build other kinds of factories, too. Our go-to-market systems run on a factory. Companies like[Translucent](https://mastra.ai/customers/translucent) have built factories for accounting.


If you're trying to get a factory in your org, we'd love to help.


## What the program entails


You'll get a software factory designed around your codebase: your repos, conventions, CI, and review process.


This includes:


- **The underlying factory, and a Slack agent that lets you operate it**
- **Forward-deployed engineers** who embed in your repo and team chat, bringing patterns from the factory we run ourselves
- **Evals and observability built-in** , so you can see what the factory is doing and prove it's working
- **Human checkpoints** so engineers approve what ships, with security and governance built-in (auth, role-based access control, etc.)


Plus you own the factory and everything it produces, and your team can operate and extend it after launch.


To get there, we start with a whiteboarding session. We want to understand your codebase and organization before we build together. Then, we'll co-embed with your team and co-build it until it's shipping PRs in production.
